newsitem.title: JAPAN: THAI REFORMS SEND STRONG SIGNAL TO MARKETS--IMF.
newsitem.headline: THAI REFORMS SEND STRONG SIGNAL TO MARKETS--IMF.

text.p: The Thai reform packages that are part of a plan to rescue its economy will send a strong signal to the financial markets, a top official with the IMF said on Monday.

"The measures they have taken and are going to take will send a good, strong signal to the market, and the Fund (IMF) management is going to propose a strong package to the highest board for its consideration," IMF deputy managing director Shigemitsu Sugisaki told Reuters Financial Television.
He also said that Malaysia and other Asian nations have taken steps to make sure that there is no spillover effect from Thailand's problems.
He said that the Thai currency crisis had "some spillover effect," but said that Malaysia and other neighbouring countries have taken appropriate measures to prevent such a crisis from spreading.
"I believe they will continue to do so (take appropriate measures) if necessary, and collective efforts will send a good signal to the market."

He said that there was a very positive response from donor nations to Thailand's presentation of its proposals at a meeting in Tokyo on Monday, noting that a total of $16 billion was pledged when Thailand had said it needed only $14 billion.
